<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="BRPXQZME" />{{running header|{{smaller|{{asc|ODE 6.}}}}|{{asc|THE MAJOR ODES OF THE KINGDOM.}}|387}}{{rule}}
{{center block/s}}</noinclude><section begin="ode5" />yellow liquid sparkling in it<ref>As a cup of such quality was the proper receptacle for the yellow, herb-flavoured spirits, so was the character of [[w:King Wen of Zhou|Wăn]] such that all blessing must accrue to him.</ref>.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Easy and self-possessed was our prince,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The fit recipient of blessing and dignity.

The hawk flies up to heaven,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The fishes leap in the deep<ref>It is the nature of the hawk to fly and of fishes to swim, and so there went out an influence from [[w:King Wen of Zhou|Wăn]] unconsciously to himself.</ref>.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Easy and self-possessed was our prince:—{{lb}}Did
he not exert an influence on men?

His clear spirits were in the vessels;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
His red bull was ready<ref>Red, we have seen, was the proper colour for victims in the [[w:Ancestral temple|ancestral temple]] of [[w:Ji (Zhou dynasty ancestral surname)|''K''âu]].</ref>;—{{lb}}To
offer, to sacrifice,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
To increase his bright happiness.

Thick grow the oaks and the buckthorn,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Which the people use for fuel<ref name="p387_4">As it was natural for the people to take the wood and use it, so it was natural for the spirits of his ancestors, and spiritual beings generally, to bless [[w:King Wen of Zhou|king Wăn]].</ref>.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Easy and self-possessed was our prince,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Cheered and encouraged by the spirits<ref name="p387_4"/>.

Luxuriant are the dolichos and other creepers,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Clinging to the branches and stems.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Easy and self-possessed was our prince,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Seeking for happiness by no crooked ways.
{{center block/e}}
<section end="ode5" />

{{c|{{sc|Ode 6. The {{tooltip|Sze ''K''âi|Sī Zhāi}}.}}}}
{{dhr|0%}}
{{smaller block/s}}
{{hanging indent/s}}
{{asc|The virtue of [[w:King Wen of Zhou|Wăn]], with his filial piety and constant reverence, and their wonderful effects. The excellent character of his mother and wife.}}
{{hanging indent/e}}
{{smaller block/e}}

{{center block/s}}
Pure and reverent was {{tooltip|Thâi ''Z''ăn|Tài Rén}}<ref>[[w:Tai Ren|Thâi ''Z''ăn]] is celebrated, above, in [[Sacred Books of the East/Volume 3/The Shih/The Major Odes of the Kingdom/Decade 1/Ode 2|the second ode]].</ref>,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The mother of king {{tooltip|Wăn|Wén}}.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Loving was she to {{tooltip|''K''âu ''K''iang|Zhōu Jiāng}}<ref name="p387_6">[[wikt:周|''K''âu]] [[wikt:姜|''K''iang]] is 'the [[w:zh:太姜|lady Kiang]]' of [[Sacred Books of the East/Volume 3/The Shih/The Major Odes of the Kingdom/Decade 1/Ode 3|ode 3]], the wife of {{tooltip|Than-fû|Dǎnfù}} or</ref>;—{{lb}}
